summary: Nine comment-endorsed developer tools, models, simulators, retro hardware projects, and media from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: zoxide
items.summary: A smarter cd command that learns which directories you visit most often.
items.why_included: A user called mapping cd to zoxide their most useful shell trick.
items.evidence: The commenter gave zoxide a strong first-hand workflow endorsement.

evidence_sources.author: disinterred
evidence_sources.excerpt: The most useful shell trick I've used to date is mapping the 'cd' command to 'zoxide', which is a more powerful version of cd that remembers folders you've been to.

items.name: Roborazzi
items.source_story_title: The Google Play app review process now regularly takes longer than a week
items.summary: An Android screenshot-testing library supporting Compose, XML views, and varied devices.
items.why_included: A production user explicitly called it an excellent screenshot library.
items.evidence: The commenter reported using Roborazzi and directly praised it.

evidence_sources.author: david_allison
evidence_sources.excerpt: We use Roborazzi[0], which is an excellent screenshot library

items.name: scikit-decide
items.summary: An Airbus-backed Python framework for planning, scheduling, and decision-making problems.
items.why_included: A commenter independently praised the linked open-source framework.
items.evidence: The commenter called scikit-decide cool and welcomed the scikit lineage.

evidence_sources.author: esafak
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's nice to see the scikit brand live on.

items.name: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5
items.summary: A sparse multimodal model with agentic capabilities and a one-million-token context window.
items.why_included: A software engineer reported excellent quality and unusually strong cost-adjusted returns.
items.evidence: The commenter uses MiMo-V2.5 for most engineering work and praised its power and ROI.

evidence_sources.author: joelwallis
evidence_sources.excerpt: I been using MiMo-V2.5 to do most of my work as software engineer, on a variety of projects I'm working on, and I been VERY happy with ROI. The model is very powerful!

items.name: GPT-5.6 Luna Max
items.summary: OpenAI's cost-efficient GPT-5.6 model running at maximum reasoning effort.
items.why_included: A Rust developer was very happy using it for asynchronous subagent reviews.
items.evidence: The commenter praised Luna Max for review work while noting that it is slow.

evidence_sources.author: rapind
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Luna Max for asynchronous subagent reviews and am very happy with its work, but it’s slow af.

items.name: FlightGear
items.source_story_title: Show HN: I made a flight simulator, except you're just a passenger
items.summary: An open-source flight simulator usable for research, training, and home simulation.
items.why_included: A flight-simulator engineer described using it in real crew-evacuation trainers.
items.evidence: The commenter reported professional deployment of FlightGear for multi-window trainer visuals.

evidence_sources.author: phugoid
evidence_sources.excerpt: We used FlightGear in a master-slave setup: the master node simulates physics and feeds accelerations to the hydraulic platform, and the slave nodes generate out-the-window visuals for each window.

items.name: MiSTer
items.source_story_title: Recreating Voodoo Graphics and a Late-1990s Gaming PC on an FPGA
items.summary: An FPGA platform recreating classic computers and consoles with hardware-level timing.
items.why_included: A commenter called it super cool and highly recommended it to retro-computing fans.
items.evidence: The commenter explicitly recommended MiSTer for people interested in old machines.

evidence_sources.author: jumploops
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's a super cool project, and I highly recommend checking it out if you have an interest in old machines (Apple II, Commodore 64, etc.).

items.name: Plagiarhythm Nation v2.0
items.source_story_title: Negativland, Culture Jamming, and the Art of Making Something New
items.summary: Evolution Control Committee's sample-heavy experimental album, available directly on Bandcamp.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended the album while discussing related culture-jamming music.
items.evidence: The commenter described Evolution Control Committee's work as wild and the linked release as good.

evidence_sources.author: cobbzilla
evidence_sources.excerpt: Evolution Control Committee had some wild stuff too in a similar vein.

items.name: AI Does to Us What American Cheese Did to Food
items.summary: An Opus 23 video essay comparing artificial intelligence with processed cheese.
items.why_included: A commenter called it the best AI video they had seen and a work of art.
items.evidence: The commenter gave the video unusually strong praise.

evidence_sources.author: verdverm
evidence_sources.excerpt: (still the best Ai video I have seen, also a work of art)
